newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line says rise in passengers, freight H1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line says rise in passengers, freight H1 '97.

text.p: Ferry operator Stena Line said on Friday that its passenger and freight volumes had risen in the first half of 1997 with volumes early in the year boosted by a fire in the channel tunnel.
Stena Line said total passenger volumes rose four percent to 7.3 million in the six months ending June 30 compared with the same period in 1996.
Stena Line says rise in passengers, freight H1 =2
Freight, measured by the number of trucks, trailers, containers and train cars, rose 18 percent over the six months to 554,000, the company said in a statement.
On English Channel routes, passenger volumes rose four percent to 3.4 million travellers and freight rose 31 percent to 259,000 units, it said.
The rise in freight on English Channel routes was "as a result of limited freight capacity on the Eurotunnel because of the tunnel fire in November 1996".
On Irish Sea routes the number of passengers rose seven percent to 1.65 million people and freight rose 18 percent to 128,300 units.
Volume developments on routes between Holyhead, Wales and Dun Laoghaire, Ireland and between Stranraer, Scotland and Belfast, Northern Ireland have been limited.
The reason is because the two high-speed HSS ferries which operate there have been in a wharf in April and May for a planned inspection, Stena Line said.

Routes between Dover, England and Calais, France and Newhaven, England and Dieppe, France will be included in the planned cross-channel joint venture between Stena Line and Peninsular and Oriental Steam Nativation Co.
Traffic volumes on routes outside these lines fell one percent and freight volumes rose eight percent.
The company will post its earnings for the six month period on August 26.
